title: Nonopposite roots of negative integer pairing have root sum
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $L,N$ be free $\mathbf Z$-modules of finite rank, meaning modules with finite bases [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $P:\operatorname{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Z\ L\ N$ be an integer root pairing: a perfect bilinear pairing $p:L\times N\to\mathbf Z$, injective families $a:I\hookrightarrow L$ and $b:I\hookrightarrow N$ with $p(a_i,b_i)=2$, and permutations $\sigma_i$ of $I$ such that $a_{\sigma_i(j)}=a_j-p(a_j,b_i)a_i$ and $b_{\sigma_i(j)}=b_j-p(a_i,b_j)b_i$. Perfect means that the induced maps $L\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(N,\mathbf Z)$ and $N\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(L,\mathbf Z)$ are isomorphisms. If $i,j\in I$, $p(a_i,b_j)<0$ and $a_i\ne-a_j$, then $a_i+a_j\in\{a_k:k\in I\}$. No reducedness or spanning assumption is required.
